blocks.text: DX Manager uses Android Developer options and ADB to run DeX and single windows for the connected phone. Enable Developer options and USB debugging on the phone first.

blocks.heading: First connection
items: Connect the phone with USB and enable USB debugging.
Allow USB debugging in the approval prompt shown on the phone.
Choose the connected phone in the DX Manager device list.

blocks.heading: If the phone has not been authorized
blocks.text: Unlock the phone and check for the USB debugging approval prompt. DeX and file transfer cannot start until the approval is granted.

DeX mode opens the Samsung DeX desktop environment. Single-window modes 1–3 each open the selected app in a separate window. Resolution, DPI, start app and launch options are saved for each phone and slot.

blocks.heading: DeX display mode
blocks.text: Choose Settings → Connection → DeX display mode. Native DeX is the default and uses the phone’s Samsung DeX environment. Simulated secondary display remains available. Stop and start DeX to apply a different mode.

blocks.heading: Start DeX or a single window
items: Select the phone and the desired mode.
Select a start app for a single window. The DeX start app is optional.
Choose display and launch options, then press Start.

blocks.heading: 120 FPS is experimental
blocks.text: Native DeX currently runs at up to 60 FPS. With Native DeX selected in Settings, choose 120 under Display settings → Max FPS in DeX mode to use simulated display for this launch after confirming. Your saved DeX mode stays unchanged. The remember checkbox is linked to the matching option in Settings. The experimental warning appears before each start, and the phone screen must stay on. Actual FPS depends on the phone and app.

blocks.heading: Single windows alongside Native DeX
blocks.text: On the same phone, single windows are limited to 60 FPS while Native DeX is active, even when 120 is selected. After stopping Native DeX, a running single window can use its configured maximum of 120 FPS.

blocks.heading: When Native DeX loses connection
blocks.text: Native DeX is cleaned up about 30 seconds after a USB or Wi-Fi disconnection is detected. Reconnecting within 30 seconds cancels cleanup and reuses the existing DeX display. If the internal display has already gone, a new one is created. The Companion app’s automatic cleanup time does not apply to Native DeX.

blocks.heading: When the phone is not listed
items: Check the USB cable and the phone's USB connection mode.
Unlock the phone and check for the USB debugging approval prompt.
Use Refresh on the main page, then choose the phone again.

blocks.text: Connect the phone and PC to the same network for Wi-Fi ADB. Check the selected connection mode and current status on the Connection page in Settings.

blocks.heading: When a session fails to launch
blocks.text: Some apps restrict launching or mirroring because of USB debugging, DRM or security policies.

topics.title: Files and DX Companion
topics.summary: Two-way transfer and optional app detection

blocks.text:
PC → phone: drag files or folders onto that phone’s scrcpy window.
Phone → PC: select files or folders in the DX Companion app, or use the Share menu in Gallery or another app.
Check destinations and transfer readiness in Settings → Paths and Settings → Companion.

blocks.heading: The Companion app is optional
blocks.text: Basic DeX and single windows work without the Companion app. To use phone-to-PC transfer, phone cleanup or app switch detection, install the matching Companion app and grant the permissions shown in Settings → Companion. App installation and accessibility activation are not automatic.

blocks.heading: AI app Enter rules and accessibility
blocks.text: Automatic line breaks for AI apps are off by default. In DX Manager, open Settings → Keyboard and enable the AI app Enter option, then enable app switch detection in the Companion app. Accessibility is optional for app detection and is not required for file transfer. Enter keeps its default behavior when app detection information is unavailable.

blocks.heading: Enable app switch detection on the phone
items: Open DX Companion app → Settings → App switch detection card.
Choose Open Accessibility settings → Installed apps.
Select DX Companion app and turn it On.

blocks.heading: Cleanup timing after disconnection
blocks.text: Companion app’s cleanup preference applies to simulated-display cleanup. Native DeX has its separate grace of about 30 seconds. Audio return to the phone and stay-awake release happen on disconnection, during that grace, while existing Bluetooth exceptions remain.

blocks.heading: Native and simulated-display cleanup
blocks.text: Native DeX is cleaned up about 30 seconds after disconnection is detected, independently of the Companion app’s timing setting. Simulated display uses the time set in the Companion app. The phone OS may end the Native DeX display earlier.
Keep the phone connected, right-click the DX Manager icon in the system tray, and choose Exit. The main window's close button hides DX Manager in the tray; it does not exit the program.

blocks.heading: If a small virtual display remains on the phone
items: Open Simulate secondary displays in Developer options on the phone.
Even if None is already selected, select any resolution once.
Open the menu again and select None.

blocks.text: With the DX Companion app installed, open its Phone cleanup tab and select Clean all to remove the display. You can also add its widget to the phone’s home screen for cleanup.
